text:
mia: FYI — running the long-context loadtest on dev-gpu-pool shows KV cache RSS creeping up over time and fragmentation ratio spikes after ~30m. I captured heap + kvslot histograms.

jon: can you drop the pprof and a short repro?

mia: pasted the trimmed output below. repro is `./tools/longrun --seq 8192 --concurrency 12 --duration 1h` against dev runtime.

praveen: pprof snippet:
```
# kv_cache_alloc histogram
size_bucket  count  bytes
64           23     1472
256          140    35840
1024         320    327680
4096         1280   5242880
16384        12     196608
```
Also hole-map scan shows many small free fragments between 512B-2KB.

sarah: that smells like our allocator is favoring one blocksize class and leaving lots of small holes. did we change default block size recently?

praveen: yes — commit abc123 (kernel-selection perf tweaks) bumped default slab block from 4KB -> 8KB to reduce kernel invocation overhead. I think that reduced allocation churn for steady loads but increased internal fragmentation for these long contexts where KV entries vary widely.

eli: interesting. eviction heuristics also were tweaked in the same window (LRU->age-bucket sampling). we might be losing reuse locality because sampling resolution dropped.

zara: short hypothesis: larger blocksize + coarser eviction sampling => small kv entries no longer pack well, leaving many tiny holes that GC/compactor rarely see.

mia: agreed. we need an actionable plan: which of these is cheapest to test? revert blocksize on canary or add mixed-size freelists?

jon: cheapest: enable mixed freelists (keep 4KB and 8KB lanes) + quick path to allocate from smaller lane when entry <2KB. if that helps we keep perf win from 8KB for big items and avoid fragmentation for small ones.

sarah: propose: segregated freelists for sizes: [<256B], [256B-2KB], [2KB-8KB], [>8KB]. bucketing can be power-of-two but bias lower for small items. also add an async minor-compaction that merges adjacent free slots when hole_ratio > 0.25.

eli: big caveat: compaction can impact p99 latency if done synchronously. we should do background compaction with rate limits and a staging buffer for copies. pseudocode: 
```
while (hole_ratio > H_THRESH && budget_ms > 0) {
  scan_bucket = pick_bucket_with_most_holes();
  coalesce(scan_bucket, budget_ms_per_iteration);
  budget_ms -= consumed;
}
```
Make budget_ms proportional to current CPU headroom.

praveen: alternative quick mitigation: change eviction sampling to keep higher-resolution for small-block classes (more samples per second). That might keep reuse and avoid creating holes long enough to need compaction. cheaper than copying.

zara: i'll prototype mixed freelists + modified sampling in dev this afternoon. will add telemetry: hole_ratio, avg_fragment_size, alloc_retry_count, p99 alloc latency.

deploy-bot: canary deployment queued: runtime-dev-canary -> image rdev/kv-fix-proto:pr-487. ETA 10m. :rocket:

jon: nice. if prototype looks promising we should run the longrun for 2h and compare rss slope and fragmentation curve vs baseline.

mia: perf budgets: p50 alloc < 150us, p99 alloc < 5ms, mem growth slope < 5MB/hour for longrun. if prototype breaches those, we fallback to reverting abc123 on canary.

praveen: i'll prepare the revert patch so we can flip quickly.

zara: taking lead on prototype. will post diffs and perf plots to thread.

mia: thanks — assign follow-ups: zara (proto + metrics), praveen (revert patch ready), jon (longrun harness + comparison dashboard), sarah (compaction alg sketch + safety limits), eli (latency-safe compaction ideas).

jon: quick question — do we want to try small-block spill buffer (preallocated pool for <512B hot items) as intermediate hack?

sarah: could be a short-term micro-optimization. low effort if we already have a small-pool impl. +1 to test after mixed-freelists.

mia: ok. timeline: prototype by EOD tomorrow, canary run for 2h once prototype built. Report in thread. :thumbsup:

zara: 👍 starting now, will tag people and paste perf graphs when ready.

mia: thanks all. closing for now — will re-open if metrics show regression.
